title: THE BEAVER IS A CIVIL ENGINEER

scenes.narration: Beavers on one Devon stream built 13 dams that hold a million litres.
scenes.title: THE BEAVER IS A CIVIL ENGINEER

scenes.narration: A beaver dam slows the stream, so sediment settles out of the water.
Suspended sediment leaving that site averaged 39 milligrams per litre, down from 112.
Storm peaks leaving the site were about 30 percent lower on average.
The ponds also lift the water table, so soil stays wet for longer.
In five US wildfires, streamside greenness fell three times less near beaver dams.
Hunting left about 1,200 beavers; Eurasia now holds at least 1.5 million.
scenes.caption: 1,200 → 1.5 M

scenes.narration: Dutch releases began in 1988, and Flanders saw beavers return around 2000. England protected beavers in 2022 and opened licensed wild releases in 2025.
Flanders went from about 150 beavers in 2013 to roughly 1,000 in 2023.
It is a trade-off, because the stored water sits on someone's farmland.
scenes.caption: A TRADE-OFF
scenes.sub: less flood risk downstream, wetter land upstream

scenes.narration: A rodent does what we pour concrete to do: slow water down. Follow for more.

Devon Wildlife Trust River Otter Beaver Trial report: dams hold up to 1 million litres; peak flows ~30% lower leaving the site; trade-off that reduced downstream flood risk can mean water stored on upstream farmland.
